decisions.reason: “Done away with” preserves the implication that the old man killed people.
SOL drops the resigned trailing “then” in 그러시다면야, 뭐.
옷소매 specifically means sleeve, not fabric generally.
BASE preserves the liquor’s potency and the scent lingering at the nose; SOL changes both to sharpness and stinging.
“Earned him a disciplinary report” naturally preserves the implied subject and consequence.
들었습니다만 is a past report—“I heard”—rather than SOL’s present-tense “I hear.”
BASE preserves “early on” and the prison-purification work; SOL weakens both details.
SOL preserves the reluctant response in more natural English word order.
“I wouldn’t say” naturally conveys the speaker’s modest denial without changing the joke.
“That’s not what I heard” is a natural spoken rendering of the old man’s rebuttal.
The omitted subject remains clear from the preceding exchange, and the clipped reply suits the dialogue.
“Really” preserves the emphasis in 별의별 while keeping the reaction idiomatic.
“Strapped to a rack” and “shitting blood” preserve the grim image in more vivid spoken English.
글쎄요 is an evasive “Did I?”/“I’m not sure,” not the more definite “Maybe.”
SOL naturally states that the prison contained dozens of cells and more than ten prisoners.
“Sympathy for them” makes the understood object explicit without changing the meaning.
BASE preserves the broader reference to “something like that”; SOL narrows it to the prisoners.
“Went into surgery” and “waiting to hear how it had gone” naturally preserve the memory and its uncertainty.
“Repeated those words to myself” and “cell door” are natural, source-faithful recasts.
“Addressed” smoothly introduces the question without changing the action.
The compressed participial construction preserves the bright expression accompanying the nod.
“The cell behind him” retains the spatial relation without redundant wording.
“Functional enough” preserves the physician’s qualified assessment naturally.
The herbs were excavated from the Cold-Ice Land and the medicines made by combining them; SOL loses both specifics.
“Give us the room” is the natural idiom for asking everyone to leave temporarily.
“Members” and “reached inside” are natural equivalents with no semantic loss.
The period cleanly separates the two system commands without changing either action.
“Safekeeping” preserves the safety rationale, and the leaner phrasing remains precise.
The source’s established title 신의 must remain “Divine Physician”; SOL replaces it with an unsupported pronoun.
SOL preserves both the emerging figure and the faint breathing while improving the sentence flow.
BASE preserves the stench and its lingering at the tip of the narrator’s nose; SOL relocates the sensation to the air.
SOL drops the unusual intensity of the chest pain and shifts the cause from Jeok’s light weight to the narrator’s realization.
“Already” naturally emphasizes the elapsed month and a half without adding a new fact.
The narrator secured treatment from the Divine Physician, not merely his general help.
“Laid him on” is idiomatic and retains the implied lowering onto the stone.
The recast preserves the provider and the stone’s therapeutic purpose naturally.
The honorific Korean subject is Jeok Cheongang; SOL incorrectly addresses him as “you.”
SOL preserves both gauntness and peacefulness in smoother prose.
“Gazed at” preserves the quiet, sustained look without changing the emotional tone.
“Everything that had happened since our first meeting” preserves the full span of remembered events.
“The more I see of you” is a natural equivalent of the repeated-looking observation.
“Clearly remembered” accurately preserves 똑똑히 and strengthens the memory detail appropriately.
SOL preserves the cherished disciple, sound roof, and tears of regret in more natural phrasing.
“Then came the year” is a natural narrative transition with the same chronology.
“Led me beyond” and “out into the vast world” preserve the movement and expansive image.
The teasing “Well?” and tag question preserve the intimate conversational tone.
피를 토하다 means vomiting blood; SOL changes the physical action to coughing it up.
SOL changes one remark on a day into plural words on one night, adding and altering details.
돌아오지 않는다 specifically means no answer came back; SOL drops that return-response nuance.
“Called to him” and “something there was to say” naturally preserve the motivation and address.
SOL adds “Of course,” an unsupported intensifier absent from the hallucinated reply.
“When it had begun” and the past perfect preserve the retrospective realization naturally.
SOL clarifies the two people’s positions while preserving the respectful salute.
“Returned my salute” naturally identifies the action’s direction without changing it.
“Assist” and “do everything in my power” preserve the young Disciple’s pledge idiomatically.
“Then leave the rest” makes the aphorism’s sequence clear without changing its meaning.
The recast preserves human effort and entrusting the remaining outcome to heaven.
The contraction matches the narrator’s intimate internal voice without changing the prayer.
“There was some … being” naturally preserves the existence claim and divine attributes.
“Spoke solemnly” is a faithful, concise equivalent of speaking in a solemn voice.
The repeated “fifteen days” is the source’s emphasis; SOL adds the unsupported qualifier “full.”
The narrator swallowed words, not explicitly a question; SOL narrows the source’s deliberate ambiguity.
The contraction preserves the vow’s force and conversational voice.
Calling the tortured man his victim accurately reflects the scene while “impassive” preserves the numb gaze.
The recast preserves the grotesque injuries and tiny voice in vivid, natural English.
The Korean is an interrogative challenge; SOL turns it into a flat assertion.
The split sentences preserve the blood, tears, and urine while improving readability.
The source says he forced out a trembling voice; SOL adds the interpretive category “plea.”
“Fading eye” naturally conveys an eye that looks ready to go out, without changing the action.
“It seems you really are telling the truth” preserves the middle-aged man’s conclusion naturally.
The recast preserves the contrast between begging for life and begging for death.
SOL adds “and gotten away with it,” changing the source’s claim that nobody had lied before him.
“No one except” is an equivalent construction that preserves the single exception.
“The extent of your half-day’s courage” naturally preserves the grim appraisal.
BASE more exactly preserves the wind sound, head movement, finger strike, and resulting death; SOL’s “thin gust” and “flicked finger” distort the action.
“Member of a collateral branch” is precise; SOL’s “collateral relative” is an awkward and potentially different category.
“Opened in the ground” naturally describes the sudden formation of the pit.
The condensed sentence preserves the five corpses, stacking, burial, and extremely short duration.
SOL adds “to me,” resolving an object the Korean leaves omitted and changing the deliberate ambiguity.
“Muttering under his breath” naturally preserves the quiet mutter and the following directional fragment.
“Purging the poison” and “cost him an arm” preserve the resistance, delay, and injury naturally.
The recast preserves vigilance, defenses, and the impossibility of attacking alone after losing an arm.
The Korean explicitly says Sichuan; SOL replaces that named location with the weaker anaphor “there.”
“Summon the hunters” is a natural equivalent of calling them in.
“As though gliding” and “the scenery swept past” preserve the supernatural speed in fluent English.
“Placed a hand against” is a precise, natural rendering of touching the cliff.
“The next instant” preserves the immediate transition without changing timing.
The reordered sentence naturally preserves the resonant hum and collapsing cliff.
The present-tense reflection and “concealed behind them” preserve the spatial revelation naturally.
기문진 is singular here; SOL incorrectly changes the established Mystic Gate Formation to plural.
SOL incorporates the preceding footsteps into a smooth movement while preserving the pattern and internal-energy action.
The following inserted hunk completes the causal sentence, and the split preserves the haze touching the pattern.
The insertion restores the precise instant at which the haze touches the pattern.
“Blazed to life” naturally conveys the pattern beginning to shine, and “entire hollow” preserves scope.
“Thunderous chorus” fits the collective shouted response immediately following and preserves its volume.
The reordered robe phrase preserves the pitch-black clothing, hunters, eyes, and blade-sharp auras.
“Touched the lips” is a natural equivalent of a faint smile forming there.
